top_finding: A 9-pipeline scheduler dropout ran for >1h and NOTHING PAGED — structurally, not by accident. At ~07:20Z nine HTTP-triggered pipelines stopped together (refresh-pack-grail-metrics-mv 113 min silent, offers-sweep 74, golazos-listings-indexer 69, pack-events-ingest 67, pack-events-ingest-backfill 60, allday-listings-indexer 59, pinnacle-events-ingest 57; golazos-sales-indexer + pinnacle-nft-resolver recovered mid-run). It is a DEGRADATION, not an outage, and partially self-healing — 60 other pipelines ran normally and sales ingest never stopped (documented cron-job.org-dropout class). The structural half: app/api/check-alerts/route.ts:186 filters alerts to critical|high and returns early otherwise, while the watchlist is 10 active high / 0 critical / 47 medium / 14 info. Of 86 pipelines running >=12x/24h, 34 have NO watchlist row and only 9 can ever page — 77 of 86 are structurally mute. Every alert emitted tonight was info. NOT framed as a dispatcher bug: severity tiers exist precisely to avoid 1am backfill pages, and bumping 61 rows to high would trade silence for alarm fatigue. The real gap is that a CORRELATED dropout is a different failure mode from any single pipeline going quiet, and nothing models it.
top_finding_2: topshot-badge-catalog cadence RESOLVED from the repo (the DB-only monitor called it undeterminable) and the answer inverts its own suggestion. .github/workflows/badge-sync.yml schedules the catalog sweep 45 2,8,14,20 * * * = 4x/day; app/api/badge-sync/route.ts:158 confirms CATALOG_PIPELINE; no vercel.json cron. Expected ~13 runs in the 3.3-day window; ACTUAL LOGGED = 2, exactly 48h apart, at 05:37Z matching none of the four slots. So the logged interval is 48h, not 6h: any threshold tight enough to be useful (720 min) pages continuously during known-broken operation, and any loose enough not to (>=2880 min) detects nothing. A watchlist row would monitor an already-failing pipeline rather than detect a new failure. Residual (GHA-visible only): is the schedule firing and the route dying before it logs, or is it not firing and something else runs at ~05:37?
